title: Disk offload provider protocol
description: The disk_offload extension point's calls (version 1, #14576; docs/server/machine-usage-map.md "Extension point disk_offload"): the manager asks a provider's program what it already holds of a computer (offload.inventory), to move items there or bring them back (offload.run, only after the user confirmed, and after the node's protection rules agreed to every path), how a job goes (offload.job) and to stop one (offload.cancel, optional: unknown_method means it cannot be canceled). Every params object carries contribution (the disk_offload item's id), locale (the caller's language: words the program writes, tool.source and detail, are in it) and machine (the computer, as a machine_section gets it). The apps read the inventory, the jobs and the manager's routes' answers (OffloadProviders, OffloadRunRequest, OffloadStarted, OffloadError) through the manager.

OffloadState.description: Whether the provider can work on this computer: ready; needs_install (its tool is not on the computer: the first offload asks to install it, OffloadTool); needs_setup (the user has to set it up first, in the extension's settings: detail says what); unavailable (detail says why).

OffloadItemKind.description: What an offloaded item was: a file, a dir (folder), an app, an app's data (app_data), a bundle of items moved together, a session archive, or other.

OffloadAction.description: What offload.run does: offload (move paths away) or restore (bring items back by id).

OffloadRunStatus.description: offload.run's answer: started (a job runs: job), needs_install (the tool is missing and install was not given: nothing happened; tool), refused (nothing happened; items say why), ok (a dry run's answer: items).

OffloadJobState.description: A job: running, done, failed (error says why) or canceled.

OffloadPhase.description: What a running job does now: install (its tool), check, upload, verify, cleanup (removing the originals), download (a restore).

OffloadJobItemStatus.description: One item of a job: pending, running, done, failed or skipped.

OffloadTool.description: The program the provider needs on the computer. source is one sentence in the caller's language saying where it comes from and where it is installed; the install confirmation shows it.

OffloadItem.description: One item the provider holds of this computer. bytes is the size it had on disk, what the map draws so both sides share one scale; stored_bytes what it takes where it is stored; origin_path where it was and where a restore puts it; stub_path the placeholder left behind, if any; local_bytes what of it is still on the computer (a cache). Times are Unix seconds.

group.description: Items moved together share a group (an app and its data).

OffloadMore.description: What the inventory left out past its 500 largest items.

OffloadInventoryParams.description: offload.inventory: what the provider holds of machine. refresh asks it not to answer from its own cache.

OffloadInventory.description: What the provider holds of the computer, largest first, at most 500 items (the rest summed in more). at is when it was read (Unix seconds); total_bytes the items' bytes together, stored_bytes what they take where they are stored; partial when the list may be incomplete. items may be left out when there are none; the manager's answer to the apps always has it.

OffloadRunParams.description: offload.run: offload paths (absolute, on machine, each already agreed by the node's protection rules) or restore items (ids of the inventory), at most 50. dry_run only checks and answers status ok with each item; install lets the job install the tool first (the user agreed to that too). request_id is the same for a retry of the same request.

OffloadRunItem.description: One path or item of a run's answer: why it is refused (reason, in the caller's language), or a dry run's verdict (ok, bytes). refusal is set only by the manager, when the computer's own protection rules refused the path before the program was asked (a machine.storage.check refusal code: credentials, app_managed, ...).

OffloadJobParams.description: offload.job and offload.cancel: the job offload.run started.

OffloadJobItem.description: One path (offload) or item (restore) of a job.

OffloadJob.description: How a job goes. A job belongs to the extension: a client that lost track asks the inventory again. items may be left out; the manager's answer to the apps always has it.

OffloadProvider.description: One enabled disk_offload contribution, as GET /api/v1/extensions/-/offload lists it for the apps.

OffloadProviders.description: GET /api/v1/extensions/-/offload?machine=: the providers the map can offer on that computer.

OffloadRunRequest.description: POST /api/v1/extensions/{id}/-/offload/{cid}/run, an app's request: without dry_run or confirm it is refused (confirmation_required); install only after the user agreed to the tool's install confirmation.

OffloadStarted.description: The run route's 202 answer: the job to follow with GET …/jobs/{job}.

OffloadError.description: An offload route's error: error in the reader's language and a code (bad_request, confirmation_required, read_only, not_found, machine_offline, node_outdated, tool_install_required with tool, offload_refused with items, plugin_failed (detail: the provider's own words, one line), usage_failed, deadline).
